sections.theory:
20.7.1.4 Conversion to Amides

Amides are the least reactive of the derivatives of carboxylic acid derivatives. These are obtained by replacing –OH of the acid with –N₂ group.

Amides can be prepared by the reaction of ammonia with carboxylic acid to form first ammonium salts which on heating produce acid amides, upon dehydration.

Amides can also be prepared by the reaction of ammonia with acid chlorides, esters or anhydrides (ammonolysis).

20.7.2 Reduction to Alcohols

Carboxylic acids can be reduced to the corresponding primary alcohol using lithium aluminum hydride in ether (Section 18.1.5.6).

20.7.3 Decarboxylation Reactions

The removal of carbon dioxide from a carboxylic acid is known as decarboxylation. Decarboxylation of carboxylic acid takes place when its sodium salt is heated with soda lime (dry mixture of caustic soda, NaOH and quick lime, CaO) to form alkanes. The resulting alkane contains one carbon less than parent carboxylic acid.

20.7.4 Reactions of Carboxylic Acid Derivatives

20.7.4.1 Reactions of Acyl Halides

Acid halides are the most reactive of all derivatives of carboxylic acid.

(i) Friedel–Crafts Acylation Reaction

Acid halides react with benzene in the presence of Lewis acid to form aromatic ketones. (Section 16.8.5.2.6).

20.7.4.2 Reactions of Acid Anhydrides

Acid Anhydrides are more reactive than esters but less reactive than acid halides, toward nucleophiles.

(i) Hydrolysis

On hydrolysis, anhydrides form corresponding carboxylic acids. The hydrolysis of anhydrides can occurs in the presence of acid or base catalyst, though uncatalyzed hydrolysis can also occurs readily.

امایډونه له اسید کلوراېډونو، ایسټرونو یا انهایدرایډونو سره د امونیا د تعامل (امونولایسس) په واسطه هم چمتو کېدای شي.

20.7.2 الکولونو ته ارجاع

کاربوکسیلیک اسیدونه په ایتر کې د لیتیم المونیم هایدراید په کارولو اړوند لومړني الکول ته ارجاع کېدای شي (برخه 18.1.5.6).

20.7.3 د ډی کاربوکسیلېشن تعاملونه

له کاربوکسیلیک اسید څخه د کاربن ډای اکساید لرې کولو ته ډی کاربوکسیلېشن وايي. د کاربوکسیلیک اسید ډی کاربوکسیلېشن هغه وخت کېږي چې د هغه سوډیم مالګه له سوډا لایم (د کاسټیک سوډا NaOH او ژوندي چونې CaO وچه ګډوله) سره توده شي، او الکانونه جوړوي. حاصل شوی الکان د اصلي کاربوکسیلیک اسید په پرتله یو کاربن کم لري.

20.7.4 د کاربوکسیلیک اسید د مشتقاتو تعاملونه

20.7.4.1 د اسایل هالایډونو تعاملونه

اسید هالایډونه د کاربوکسیلیک اسید په ټولو مشتقاتو کې تر ټولو ډېر تعامل کوونکي دي.

(i) د فریډل–کرافټس اسایلېشن تعامل

اسید هالایډونه د لیوس اسید په شتون کې له بنزین سره تعامل کوي او اروماتیک کیټونونه جوړوي. (برخه 16.8.5.2.6).

20.7.4.2 د اسید انهایدرایډونو تعاملونه

اسید انهایدرایډونه د نیوکلیوفایلونو په وړاندې له ایسټرونو ډېر خو له اسید هالایډونو لږ تعامل کوونکي دي.

(i) هایدرولایسس

د هایدرولایسس پر مهال انهایدرایډونه اړوند کاربوکسیلیک اسیدونه جوړوي. د انهایدرایډونو هایدرولایسس د اسیدي یا قلوي کتلست په شتون کې کېدای شي، که څه هم بې کتلسته هایدرولایسس هم په اسانۍ کېږي.

20.7.1.4 Conversion to Amides

Amides are the least reactive of the derivatives of carboxylic acid derivatives. These are obtained by replacing –OH of the acid with –N₂ group.

Amides can be prepared by the reaction of ammonia with carboxylic acid to form first ammonium salts which on heating produce acid amides, upon dehydration.

Amides can also be prepared by the reaction of ammonia with acid chlorides, esters or anhydrides (ammonolysis).

20.7.2 Reduction to Alcohols

Carboxylic acids can be reduced to the corresponding primary alcohol using lithium aluminum hydride in ether (Section 18.1.5.6).

20.7.3 Decarboxylation Reactions

The removal of carbon dioxide from a carboxylic acid is known as decarboxylation. Decarboxylation of carboxylic acid takes place when its sodium salt is heated with soda lime (dry mixture of caustic soda, NaOH and quick lime, CaO) to form alkanes. The resulting alkane contains one carbon less than parent carboxylic acid.

20.7.4 Reactions of Carboxylic Acid Derivatives

20.7.4.1 Reactions of Acyl Halides

Acid halides are the most reactive of all derivatives of carboxylic acid.

(i) Friedel–Crafts Acylation Reaction

Acid halides react with benzene in the presence of Lewis acid to form aromatic ketones. (Section 16.8.5.2.6).

20.7.4.2 Reactions of Acid Anhydrides

Acid Anhydrides are more reactive than esters but less reactive than acid halides, toward nucleophiles.

(i) Hydrolysis

On hydrolysis, anhydrides form corresponding carboxylic acids. The hydrolysis of anhydrides can occurs in the presence of acid or base catalyst, though uncatalyzed hydrolysis can also occurs readily.
